body:
The run for task:21241abf8e6ac8a7 started in the plain root project, and its first `Next` call named `mcp.tool_schema` and `board.work_role` instead of any Store code. Both come from `store_read.Store::named`: it only finds names written `module.name`, so a task that names `Store` bare is invisible to `board.start_project` and to the session ranking.

Treat a backticked bare identifier as a name when it resolves to exactly one symbol. That should choose the project that holds the named code and boost those symbols in `session start --task`. Common words and ambiguous bare names must not count, and the existing `module.name` behavior stays.

Tests:
- a task scoped to `.` and `solace-cli` whose body says `Store` starts in `solace-cli`;
- its first call names a Store symbol;
- a bare word matching several symbols neither chooses a project nor outranks named code.

For investigation to answer: is this actually a good idea to implement?
title: briefs: start from the task's code
